free_tier.stated: No published per-package or total quota found on the upload page or the server API. Uploads are permanent: 'Upload and publish a package permanently' and 'You can only upload a package version once and this cannot be undone'. Real large package verified: pandoc-3.5.tar.gz is 7,483,625 bytes. Packages must be `cabal sdist` output (gzipped tar with package.cabal).

retention.stated: No published per-package or total quota found on the upload page or the server API. Uploads are permanent: 'Upload and publish a package permanently' and 'You can only upload a package version once and this cannot be undone'

egress.terms: Free. Content is served from hackage.haskell.org and the hackage-content.haskell.org CDN. No billing, no bandwidth meter.

record.tooling: `cabal upload` / `stack upload` (write), `hup` (a dedicated upload client, hackage.haskell.org/package/hup), Hackage server API at hackage-origin.haskell.org/api (open, 62,403-byte route listing), plain HTTPS tarball GET (read).
record.chaining: unlimited packages x unlimited versions per package (versions are never deleted and the index keeps all of them) x unlimited free Hackage accounts. Content must be a Cabal sdist, but the sdist can contain arbitrary files declared in extra-source-files - so a multi-GB blob can be shipped as a package's data. Multiply: N accounts x M packages x K versions.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none documented; 7.4 MB verified, and the 100 MB-class limits seen in other ecosystems are not stated here - likely a server-side request size limit that is undocumented. IMPORTANT retention property: uploads are immutable and permanent (no delete, no re-upload of the same version), which is exactly what an archive workload wants. request-rate: not documented.
record.reliability_note: Immutable by design - a bad upload cannot be deleted, which is irreversibility risk in the other direction. No documented byte ceiling means the ceiling is empirical and could change without notice. Read path is plain static files and reliable.
